questions.stem: Which of the following leads to an increase in enzyme activity?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase in temperature above the optimum

questions.solutionHtml:
Decrease in activation energy
  • For a substrate to become a product, it goes to a transition state (S‡) which is a fleeting, momentary, unstable chemical species that is neither substrate nor product.
  • This species has the highest free energy in a reaction coordinate diagram. This creates an energy barrier for a substrate to become a product. This energy is known as activation energy.
  • So, activation energy is the free energy difference between substrates and that of their transition state

Gibb’s Free Energy graph for enzyme-catalyzed and enzyme uncatalyzed reaction. On X-axis, reaction progress is taken (i.e. S getting converted to P). For any spontaneous reaction, S has more free energy as compared to P. For S to be converted to P, first S has to acquire activation energy and reach a high energy state (transition state). Only then it can be converted to P.

  • The enzyme acts by decreasing the free energy of the transition state intermediate by its stabilization, so that activation energy also decreases.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 32nd Edition, Page No. 72-73

questions.stem: All of the following statements about enzymes are true EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: Multienzyme complexes greatly reduce the rates of reactions

options.label: B
options.text: Isoenzymes differ in their amino acid sequence

options.label: C
options.text: Allosteric regulators do not bind to the active site of the enzyme

options.label: D
options.text: Translational regulation is the method of long-term regulation of enzymatic activity

questions.answerText: Multienzyme complexes greatly reduce the rates of reactions
questions.solutionHtml:
Multienzyme complexes greatly reduce the rates of reactions
  • Multienzyme complex: Stable, non-valent assembly of different enzymes involved in consecutive reactions of a metabolic pathway e.g. PDH complex, α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex.
  • They greatly increase the rate of reactions as the product of one enzyme serves as a reactant for the next enzyme in the complex. This reduces the time for diffusion of substrates to another site in the cell, hence reaction becomes faster (so, option a is the wrong statement).



Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 6th edition page no. 602

questions.stem: Cytochrome Oxidase is an enzyme carrying out the transfer of electrons to the final electron acceptor O2 in ETC. The presence of which of the following is required for the proper working of this enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Both A & B

Cytochrome oxidase

  • Cytochrome oxidase aka complex IV of ETC consists of a superfamily of proteins that act as the terminal enzymes of respiratory chains in a variety of organisms. It transfers electrons from cytochrome c to the final electron acceptor O2.
  • Structural features of human cytochrome oxidase:
    • It is a large multi-subunit complex with multiple heme proteins and Cu ions forming Fe-Cu centers for the transfer of electrons.
    • Electron transfer through Complex IV is from cytochrome c to the CuA center, to heme a, to the heme a3–CuB center, and finally to O2


Textbook of Biochemistry by Vasudevan 7th Edition Page No. 67

questions.stem: Aldehyde dehydrogenase an enzyme involved in the metabolism of alcohol requires NAD+ for its proper function. Here NAD+ can be most appropriately termed as:
questions.solutionHtml:
Coenzyme
  • NAD+ is an organic non-protein portion that is required for the enzyme, so it is a coenzyme.
  • Examples of other coenzymes are FAD, NADP, PLP, TPP, etc.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 32nd Edition, Page No. 61

questions.stem: A number of mechanisms are used by enzymes for increasing the rate of a reaction. Which of the following is NOT employed by enzymes for catalysis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Increasing activation energy
  • Enzymes increase the rate of reaction by decreasing the activation energy (Option C is false).
  • It does so by lowering the free energy of the transition state, so that the transition state will be reached faster compared to a non-catalyzed reaction.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 32nd Edition, Page No. 61-63

questions.stem: Trypsin is a serine protease that cleaves proteins by the addition of water. In a polypeptide, it will act and cleave at the carboxy-terminal of which of the following amino acids?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arginine
  • Trypsin is a serine protease as it has a serine at its active site
  • Trypsin cleaves a polypeptide at the carboxy-terminal of basic amino acids arginine and lysine (see fig).
  • Amino acid triad in the active site of serine proteases consists of serine, histidine, and aspartate.
  • Examples of serine proteases: Chymotrypsin, Trypsin, Elastase, Thrombin, Plasmin, Complements, Factors X and XI
  • Serine Proteases differ in substrate specificity




Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 7th edition page no. 215

questions.stem: If the Serine amino acid residue present at the active site of Chymotrypsin is changed with Proline. Which of the following will happen?

options.label: A
options.text: Chymotrypsin can catalyze the protein hydrolysis but cannot bind it

options.label: B
options.text: Chymotrypsin can bind the protein but cannot catalyze its hydrolysis

options.label: C
options.text: Chymotrypsin can bind as well as can catalyze the protein hydrolysis

options.label: D
options.text: Chymotrypsin can neither bind nor can catalyze the protein hydrolysis

questions.answerText: Chymotrypsin can bind the protein but cannot catalyze its hydrolysis
questions.solutionHtml:
Chymotrypsin can bind the protein but cannot catalyze its hydrolysis
  • Chymotrypsin is a serine protease with a catalytic triad of serine, histidine, and aspartate at its active site.
  • During the catalysis of hydrolysis of the peptide bond, the enzyme first binds the substrate through histidine and arginine. Then the hydrolysis of the peptide bond takes place with the participation of serine residue.
  • The question says that a site-specific/directed mutagenesis (oligonucleotide with single base change- UCA (serine) changes to CCA (proline)) is done.
  • Histidine and Aspartate residues have the function of binding to peptide/protein substrate. As these amino acids are not changed, so, the enzyme will be able to bind (options A and D are false)
  • But the hydrolysis is done by serine residue, so, the mutated enzyme in which serine is replaced with proline will not be able to catalyze the hydrolysis (option C is false).




Lehninger Principles of biochemistry 6th edition page no. 215

questions.stem: Vitamins and their derivatives constitute a majority of biological coenzymes. Which of the following is a Non-vitamin coenzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lipoic acid
  • It is an organosulfur compound formed from precursor octanoic acid (an 8C fatty acid) in the body so, it is not a vitamin.
  • Lipoic acid acts as a coenzyme for enzymes pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase and is attached by a strong covalent bond.
  • Another Non-vitamin coenzyme is Tetrahydrobiopterin derived from guanosine triphosphate.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 32nd Edition, Page No. 98

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly defines Isoenzymes?

options.label: A
options.text: Forms of the same enzyme that catalyze the different reaction

options.label: B
options.text: Forms of the same enzyme that catalyze the same reaction

options.label: C
options.text: Forms of the different enzymes that catalyze the different reaction

options.label: D
options.text: Forms of the different enzymes that catalyze the same reaction

questions.answerText: Forms of the same enzyme that catalyze the same reaction
questions.solutionHtml:
Forms of the same enzyme that catalyze the same reaction
  • Isozymes/Isoenzymes are different forms of the same enzyme, catalyzing the same reaction in the same species (Options A and C are false)
  • For example, there are five isozymes of Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH-1 to LDH-5), All convert Pyruvate to Lactate.
  • So, for isoenzymes, the reaction and species will always be the same.



Lehninger Principles of biochemistry 6th edition page no. 602

questions.stem: Isoenzymes can be differentiated from each other by
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above

Identification of Isoenzymes:

  1. In polyacrylamide gel or agar gel electrophoresis, the isoenzymes have different mobility due to the difference in their MW. LDH, CK, and ALP isoenzymes can be separated by electrophoresis (Option A is true).
  2. Heat stability: One of the isoenzymes may be easily denatured by heat, e.g. bone isoenzyme of ALP (BALP) while other liver ALP is much more heat stable (Option B is true)
  3. Inhibitors: One of the isoenzymes may be sensitive to one inhibitor, e.g. tartrate labile ACP (ACP-1, 2, 3 and 6) vs Tartrate resistant ACP (TRAP) ACP-5
  4. Km value or substrate specificity may be different for isoenzymes, e.g. glucokinase has high Km and hexokinase has low Km for glucose. Glucokinase specifically acts on glucose as a substrate while hexokinase can phosphorylate any hexose sugar (Option C is true).
  5. Co-factor requirements can be different for isoenzymes, for example, the cytoplasmic isoenzyme of isocitrate dehydrogenase is NADP+ dependent whereas Mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase is NAD+ dependent.
  6. Tissue localization may be different for isoenzymes. The H4 form of LDH is present in the heart, while the M4 variety is present in skeletal muscle.
  7. Specific antibodies may identify different types of isoenzymes. For example, CK isoenzymes are separated by different antibodies.



Textbook of Biochemistry by Vasudevan 7th Edition Page No. 83

questions.stem: Argininosuccinate synthetase (EC 6.3.4.5) links aspartate and citrulline via the amino group of aspartate and provides the second nitrogen of urea. The reaction requires ATP and involves the intermediate formation of citrullyl-AMP. Subsequent displacement of AMP by aspartate then forms argininosuccinate.Select the class of enzyme that the enzyme belongs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ligases

Argininosuccinate synthetase (EC 6.3.4.5) belongs to ligases. Argininosuccinate synthase or synthetase is an enzyme that catalyzes the synthesis of argininosuccinate from citrulline and aspartate.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry: 32nd Edition, Page No. 286

questions.stem: Glucokinase is an enzyme that facilitates the phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate. It plays an important role in the regulation of carbohydrate metabolism by acting as a glucose sensor, triggering shifts in metabolism or cell function in response to rising or falling levels of glucose.Select the appropriate class of enzyme to which glucokinase belong?
questions.solutionHtml:
Transferase

Glucokinase (GK) is a hexokinase isozyme, related homologously to at least three other hexokinases. All of the hexokinases can mediate the phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate (G6P), which is the first step of both glycogen synthesis and glycolysis.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 165
